text:
pagerbot: PAGER: auth-service alert — unexpected 401 spike + high egress to staging log bucket (rule: auth.unusual_401_high_egress). Please acknowledge.

sanjay: acked. looking now.

elaine: oncall here, pinged infra traces. can we confirm customer impact?

ops-oncall: quick check — production token validation latency is fine, but we're seeing lots of failed refresh attempts from a small IP range. not yet seeing successful data reads.

ben: noticed S3 PUTs to a staging debug bucket around the same time. sample path: staging-logs/auth/2026/03/18/part-0003.log

security: creating SEC ticket INC-2026-042 in 3..2..1. tagging legal.

security: initial triage: logs include truncated auth header snippets (bearer prefixes only), no full tokens observed in first pass. still treating as sensitive.

katie: legal on standby. need customer comms if any PII exposed.

elaine: copying sample (sanitized) entry: "[2026-03-18T14:05:12Z] auth.failed refresh user=alice path=/v1/generate ip=203.0.113.45 header=Bearer..."

ops-oncall: running quick search on s3 bucket for matching keys and size anomalies.

ops-oncall: found ~12 files with auth snippets, all in staging prefix, uploaded by ci-batch role.

sanjay: that suggests CI forwarder misconfigured rather than prod compromise. who owns the CI forwarder? @infra-cicd?

ben: infra-cicd is offline today; last deploy by terraform job "ci-forwarder-2" on 2026-03-17 23:58 UTC.

security: timeline: 03-17 23:58 Terraform deploy -> 03-18 14:03 burst of failed refreshes -> 14:05 logs pushed. Looks like a misrouted debug sink.

ops-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) block suspicious IP range at edge WAF rule, 2) revoke and rotate any service creds used by ci-forwarder role, 3) remove exposed files from staging bucket and preserve copies for forensics in secure storage. executing now.

elaine: executing step 1: adding WAF rule now. Rule id: waf-block-1934. ETA ~2m.

pagerbot: deploybot: WAF change applied by elaine at 2026-03-18T14:12:20Z.

sanjay: executing step 2: rotating ci-forwarder AWS key pair and invalidating old sessions. new access key created and stored in vault. rotation completed at 2026-03-18T14:18Z.

security: step 3 started — copying affected objects to forensic bucket s3://redwood-forensics/INC-2026-042/ then deleting originals from staging. checksum verified.

katie: legal wants statement draft if customers affected. recommend: "no evidence of customer keys or full tokens in leaked files; items contained to staging debug bucket created by CI forwarder; credentials rotated and mitigation complete; ongoing review."

ben: double-checking logs for prod paths: grep across prod buckets came up negative for auth snippets.

ops-oncall: customer impact assessment: currently none observed for production. potential exposure limited to the staging debug bucket. severity: low-medium until forensics complete.

security: marking incident as contained for now. continuing investigation into CI job config (why debug headers were forwarded). assigning long-term action to infra-cicd: add header-scrub step to forwarder and deny write to any non-prod buckets unless explicitly permitted.

elaine: handing off to night oncall @sanjay for 2h watch. I will update runbook and incident ticket with actions.

sanjay: taking watch. leaving subset of checks on a 15m cron: 1) search for auth header snippets in buckets, 2) WAF hit rate, 3) unexpected token validation errors.

legal: thanks. please ping if any customer DMs necessary.

security: next steps: full CI job audit, rotate any downstream keys touched by forwarder (list attached in ticket), postmortem scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PT.

pagerbot: NOTE: if any new successful token reuse is detected, escalate to pager with priority=high.

elaine: closing bridge. thanks team, good job moving fast. :thumbsup:
